bihar_raw_news.title: 'Our promise: Predictable policy regime and power subsidies,' says Finmin Swapan ...
bihar_raw_news.content: West Bengal Finmin Swapan Dasgupta at ET Bengal Ascends West Bengal is looking to rebuild investor confidence by addressing concerns over land availability, labour practices and business environment, and restore economic growth because "nothing succeeds like success," state finance minister Swapan Dasgupta told Deepshikha Sikarwar during a fireside chat at ET Bengal Ascends . He discussed the challenge of tackling labour syndication, bringing skilled talent back to the state and managing debt of around ₹8 lakh crore. Also Read | ET Bengal Ascends: CM Suvendu Adhikari pitches a middle path to unlock land for industry Edited excerpts: Your government came to power six months back. How has the experience been of the 'double-engine' sarkar? Live Events There is a lot of curiosity, a lot of expectation, a lot of optimism and goodwill shown by the people who for different reasons with great regret left West Bengal. They are the people who are providing the goodwill and impetus for revival and telling us you got to do something. That itself is the most reassuring part of our job in the past six months. You said the narrative about Bengal needs a change. What does Bengal ascending look like for the next five years? How do you break this narrative? Firstly, nothing succeeds like success. What we need is to immediately tell people that there is hope, it is not inevitable that all the young people in West Bengal will leave the state, and that it is possible for investment to come into West Bengal. It is possible for entrepreneurs within the state to actually do well. So, you ought to create systems. Also Read | ET Bengal Ascends: From luchi to boardroom deals, Kolkata serves up a feast of ambition One of the biggest tragedies was that for four-five decades, a large part of the government and institutions associated with the government remained aloof from what happened in the rest of India. The progressive changes happened in India since the early 1990s... We missed the bus totally. Yesterday, we finally got the repeal of the Urban Land Ceiling Act approved at the cabinet. Now, we need to go to the assembly and get it done...by the end of the year. The abolition of urban land ceiling is just one step. The next one - acquisition of land in rural areas for industry - is difficult because of complex tenancy laws. Those things have to be changed. You need political muscle and political confidence to be able to do that. I believe the repeal of the urban land ceiling act will trigger a real estate boom...and that will take real estate out of the hands of people who just monopolise and terrorise people. Once the organised sector comes in line with what is happening in the rest of the country, things will fall in place. Land has been one of the key concerns for the investors in West Bengal, especially after the Singur episode. How do you plan to address investors' concerns?

national_raw_news.title: India to mark Constitution Day on November 26
national_raw_news.content: The Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) will be observed tomorrow to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November, 1949. The day has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015. Constitution Day provides an occasion to reflect upon the principles and values enshrined in the Constitution of India and to renew the collective commitment to its ideals. The observance seeks to strengthen constitutional awareness, promote responsible citizenship and encourage active participation in upholding the democratic values of the nation. On the occasion, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs is facilitating an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, comprising 22 Scheduled Languages and English. This initiative will provide an opportunity to citizens across the country to read the Preamble and reaffirm their commitment to the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution. Various activities are being organised across the country by Ministries and Departments of the Government, State and Union Territories Governments, autonomous bodies and institutions to mark the occasion. These activities include collective reading of the Preamble, seminars, webinars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, poster-making, cultural programmes, awareness campaigns, walks, runs and other community engagement activities. The Ministry noted that various awareness and outreach activities are also being undertaken through digital platforms and community-based initiatives to promote understanding of the Constitution and its significance in the country’s democratic framework.

national_raw_news.title: Constitution Day to Be Observed Across India on November 26
national_raw_news.content: Constitution Day, or Samvidhan Diwas, will be observed across the country on November 26 to mark the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949. The day has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015 to promote awareness about the Constitution and reaffirm the country’s commitment to its democratic values and principles. As part of this year’s celebrations, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs is facilitating an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, including 22 Scheduled Languages and English. Citizens can participate by reading the Preamble, downloading a participation certificate and sharing it on social media. The celebrations also include a Constitution Quiz being conducted through the MyGov and MyBharat portals from November 18 to 26. In addition, Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad is being organised across 786 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories from November 24 to 26 to encourage greater participation among young people. Several activities are being organised by Central Ministries and Departments, State and Union Territory governments, educational institutions and other organisations. These include collective readings of the Preamble, seminars, webinars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, poster-making, cultural programmes, awareness campaigns, walks and community engagement initiatives. Schools, colleges and universities have also been encouraged to organise special morning assemblies, discussions and competitions to familiarise students with the making of the Constitution and its key features. With a special focus on grassroots participation, the celebrations aim to strengthen constitutional awareness among citizens, particularly young people and students, through digital platforms and community-based outreach programmes. Constitution Day serves as an occasion to reflect on the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity enshrined in the Constitution and renew the collective commitment to upholding the country’s democratic framework.

national_raw_news.title: PM chairs 55th PRAGATI meeting
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister's Office PM chairs 55th PRAGATI meeting PM reviews five infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors worth over ₹78,000 crore PM stresses on timely execution accompanied by high standards of construction quality PM also reviews the ITI ecosystem including the implementation of PM-SETU PM calls for stronger PSU–ITI linkages and skilling aligned with industrial clusters and sectoral needs PM advocates the 3C approach of Classroom–Company–Career to connect training with employment PM notes that stronger links between ITIs and local employers could expand employment opportunities closer to home Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the 55th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth earlier today. The platform brings together the Central and State Governments to address implementation bottlenecks and improve the delivery of projects and welfare schemes. During the meeting, the Prime Minister reviewed five critical infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors, with a total cost of over ₹78,000 crore. He also reviewed the Industrial Training Institute (ITI) ecosystem, including the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU). Prime Minister emphasised that delays in infrastructure projects have consequences beyond cost escalation, as they postpone the benefits intended for citizens, businesses and the economy. He called upon the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve pending issues with clear responsibility and realistic timelines. He stressed that timely execution must be accompanied by high standards of construction quality. Reviewing the road project, the Prime Minister called for expeditious implementation and reiterated the need to focus on outcomes over outlays. While reviewing the coal project, the Prime Minister emphasised that rehabilitation and resettlement should be undertaken in a timely and dignified manner alongside timely project implementation. While reviewing the power project, the Prime Minister suggested exploring innovative models for decentralised solar and wind power projects. He emphasised that such projects should be developed closer to centres of consumption wherever feasible, taking into account local resource availability and demand. These efforts should aim to improve the availability of reliable and affordable power and ease pressure on transmission infrastructure. Reviewing the ITI ecosystem and the implementation of PM-SETU, Prime Minister called upon Chief Ministers and Chief Secretaries to provide leadership in strengthening ITIs and deepening industry participation under PM-SETU. He emphasised that this was an opportune time for industry to partner with ITIs, contribute to their upgradation and help align training with current and future manpower requirements. He called for close collaboration between States, ITIs and industry to translate these partnerships into better training and employment opportunities for young people. Prime Minister called upon Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to assess their future manpower requirements and strengthen linkages with ITIs for training and recruitment in relevant trades.
